title: Preparation of 3D Collagen Gels and Microchannels for the Study of 3D Interactions In Vivo
protocol: Neutralize collagen (1:1) with sterile, ice-cold 100 mM HEPES in 2x PBS, pH 7.4.
Mix thoroughly until solution is homogenous and mixing swirls are no longer visible.
Dilute neutralized collagen to the appropriate concentration with cell media.
Calculate the amount of neutralized collagen required using N = (D*V)/(S/2).
Bring up the amount of neutralized collagen to volume by adding a cell and cell media solution.
Mix thoroughly until homogeneous.
Store on ice until ready to cast.
Pipet the ice-cold collagen/cell/media mixture into a non-tissue culture treated 6-well plate or a 50 mm glass bottom dish.
Use a pipet tip to evenly spread out the solution.
Allow the mixture to polymerize at room temperature for approximately 10 - 15 minutes.
Move the plate or dish to 37 °C after the gels have turned opaque, and allow further polymerization for 45 - 60 minutes.
Add 2 - 3 ml of media after the polymerization period.
Run a p200 pipet tip around the perimeter of the well or dish to release the gels from the sides.
Swirl the dish gently to ensure the gel is floating in the media.
Mix PDMS thoroughly in a disposable cup with a craft stick.
De-gas the PDMS mixture by placing the disposable cup in a vacuum chamber under a vacuum pressure of 550 mm Hg.
Prepare the silicone master for pouring by placing a clean sheet of transparency film onto a hotplate followed by the silicone master, ensuring that the microchannel mold faces up.
Pour de-gassed PDMS over the silicone master carefully to avoid air bubbles.
Apply a second sheet of transparency film on top of the PDMS/silicone master to avoid air bubbles.
Roll the second transparency sheet down on top of the PDMS/silicone master gently.
Place a rubber sheet on top of the transparency, followed by a 1/8" acrylic sheet.
Add three 10 lb weights on top of the acrylic sheet.
Set hotplate temperature to 70 °C and cure PDMS for 4 hr.
Allow PDMS to cool for at least 1 additional hr before handling.
Peel top sheet of transparency film from the wafer using a forceps.
Carefully remove channels with a forceps.
Store channels in a dust-free dish until ready to use.
Place channels upside down on new, clean transparency film.
Clean all ports (Figure 2b) using circular motion with a sharp forceps.
Remove any PDMS fragments during cleaning.
Clean channels by pressing onto sticky side of packing tape.
Press down on channels with round end of forceps to ensure good contact.
Repeat the cleaning process until visible debris is removed from both sides.
Transfer cleaned, prepped PDMS channels into a 50 ml conical tube containing 70% EtOH.
Vortex at maximum speed for 30 sec.
Discard 70% EtOH and replace with fresh 70% EtOH.
Store in 70% EtOH until ready to use.
Transfer the PDMS channels into a clean and sterile cover glass or glass bottom dishes under aseptic techniques in tissue culture hood.
UV treat the PDMS channels until EtOH has evaporated completely.
Flip the PDMS so that channels are facing down toward the coverglass.
Press the PDMS channel down on the glass to create a good seal.
Add a patch of sterile PDMS to cover/close the center port (port B, Figure 2b).
Allow the setup to thoroughly dry before proceeding.
Pre-coat the inside of the channel with 10 µg/ml collagen in sterile water.
Place a 100 μl droplet on the top of a channel and draw through with vacuum.
Incubate at 37 °C for 1 hour.
Transfer channels filled with collagen coating solution to a refrigerator.
Chill for approximately 15 - 30 minutes.
Remove collagen coating solution using an aspirator or pipet.
Neutralize collagen (1:1) on ice with ice-cold 100 mM HEPES in 2x PBS, pH 7.4.
Mix thoroughly until homogenous.
Dilute neutralized collagen to the appropriate concentrations with cell media.
Incubate for 15 minutes on ice.
Chill mounted channels on ice simultaneously.
Count cells with a hemacytometer and resuspend at the appropriate seeding density.
Resuspend cells to 1 - 3 million cells/ml.
Pour aligned and random collagen microchannels once cells have been counted and 15 min have passed.
Adjust vacuum pressure using an inline vacuum regulator.
Use a wide channel (3mm x 200 µm) for random matrices with a vacuum pressure of 10 mm Hg or less.
Use a narrow channel (1mm x 200 µm) for aligned matrices with a vacuum pressure of 60 mm Hg or greater.
Remove mounted channel from ice and place on clean, sanitized surface in the laminar flow hood.
Load 120 - 150 µl of neutralized collagen into port A.
Place a 25 ml pipet attached to the vacuum line over port C.
Draw collagen through the channel by placing the pipet over port C.
For random matrices, draw collagen slowly (approximately 0.5 - 1 mm per second).
For aligned matrices, draw the collagen more rapidly while avoiding air bubbles.
Remove excess collagen from ports A and C with a p200 pipetman or aspirator.
Cover both ports A and C with sterile PDMS patches.
Mix 2 - 3 μl of cells (5 - 10 thousand cells) into the center port after 2 - 3 minutes.
Allow the mixture to partially polymerize at room temperature for another 10 - 15 min.
Transfer to 37 °C for additional 15 - 30 min to finish polymerization.
Remove PDMS covers and add media to completely cover the channel.
Feed cells by removing 1 ml of old media and replacing it with 1 ml of new media.
